environment.description: Same application deployed behind Envoy service mesh with an external authorization filter (ext_authz) pointing to a custom OPA bundle. The OPA policy (package docvault.authz) evaluates a Rego rule that performs a real-time lookup against the document ownership table via a cached data.documents binding refreshed every 5s from PostgreSQL. The rule denies any request where input.parsed_path[2] (the documentId path segment) resolves to a document whose owner_id field does not match input.metadata["x-user-id"] AND the requesting user is not in the document's share_acl array. Additionally, the CloudHSM key policy (managed via AWS KMS custom key store) includes a condition key 'kms:ViaService' restricting signing operations to requests originating from the pod service account ARN that also carries an SVID matching the caller's authenticated identity - meaning even if OPA were bypassed, the HSM would refuse to sign a pre-signed URL unless the SPIFFE identity in the mTLS connection matches the document owner or an authorized sharer. The Envoy ext_authz filter is configured with failure_mode_allow: false, meaning if OPA is unreachable, all requests are denied.

config.service_mesh: Envoy 1.28 with ext_authz gRPC filter, failure_mode_allow: false
config.opa_policy: package docvault.authz; default allow = false; allow { doc := data.documents[input.parsed_path[2]]; doc.owner_id == input.metadata["x-user-id"] } allow { doc := data.documents[input.parsed_path[2]]; input.metadata["x-user-id"] == doc.share_acl[_] }
config.opa_data_sync: PostgreSQL -> OPA bundle server, 5s refresh interval, documents table
config.spiffe: SPIRE agent issues SVIDs; HSM signing proxy validates caller SVID against document ACL before forwarding sign request to CloudHSM
config.envoy_config: ext_authz { grpc_service { envoy_grpc { cluster_name: "opa-authz" } } failure_mode_allow: false; with_request_body { max_request_bytes: 8192 } }
